title: Grateful Dead Live at Family Dog at the Great Highway on 1969-08-29
venue: Family Dog at the Great Highway
lineage: SBD > MR > C > D > CD > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard mix captures a fiery early Dead set with standout Casey Jones, Easy Wind and the rare New Orleans → Searchin' → Good Lovin' sequence.
ai_review.review: The recording is a high‑quality stereo soundboard capture that sounds surprisingly clean for 1969, with a perfect mix that lets the gritty organ and dirty guitars shine. Musically the show is praised for its early Working Man’s vibe, featuring a scorching Casey Jones, an organ‑heavy Easy Wind, a rare New Orleans → Searchin' → Good Lovin' medley, plus four Pigpen‑led numbers including a marathon Turn On Your Love Light. Overall reviewers are enthusiastic, noting both the performance energy and the superb audio fidelity.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently high star ratings (mostly 4‑5) and detailed praise for both musical performance and recording quality lead to a strong combined rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: High‑quality stereo audio, perfect mix for the era, clear yet nicely dirty sound; organ presence noted, overall clean and balanced.

standout_songs: Turn On Your Love Light (30:55 version)
show_quality.setlist_flow: Early Working‑Man transition set with strong pigpen showcases and a rare, high‑energy medley that keeps the momentum flowing from the first to the second half.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Lead vocals on Good Lovin', shines on Easy Wind, guitar tone praised; noted for kicking in hard during Good Lovin'.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass and drums together “kill” on Good Lovin'; praised for solid rhythm foundation.
band_member_comments.Bob: Provides tight backing vocals (especially on Good Lovin'); backup vocal support highlighted.
band_member_comments.Keys: Heavy organ presence on Easy Wind, likely Tom Constanten near the end of his tenure; keyboards described as ‘dirty’ and essential to the sound.
band_member_comments.Drums: Drummers praised for driving the groove, especially on Good Lovin' where they lock in with Jerry’s vocal entrance.
